docs.title: Stash Sense
docs.text: ML-powered performer identification and library curation for Stash.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
• Identifies performers in scenes and images using face recognition against a database of 108,000+ performers sourced from multiple Stash-Box endpoints
  • Tags scenes from Stash-Box by searching untagged scenes across Stash-Box endpoints using file fingerprints
  • Detects duplicate scenes using face fingerprints, Stash-Box IDs, and metadata overlap — catches duplicates that phash matching misses
  • Syncs upstream changes from Stash-Box endpoints with per-field merge controls for performers, studios, and scenes
  • Runs locally on your hardware — no cloud dependencies, no data leaves your network

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Stash Sense has three components that work together:

  • Stash — Your media organizer (already running). Stash Sense reads your library data and writes back performer tags, metadata updates, etc.
  • Stash Sense Sidecar — A Docker container running ML models and analysis engines. It connects to Stash via API key and handles all the heavy lifting (face recognition, upstream diffing, duplicate detection).
  • Stash Sense Plugin — Installed inside Stash, provides the UI (dashboard, settings, scene-level controls). It talks to the sidecar through a backend proxy.

Stash-Box endpoints (StashDB, FansDB, ThePornDB, etc.) are configured in Stash's Settings > Metadata Providers — the sidecar reads credentials from there automatically.

Next steps:

  • Installation — Docker setup, plugin install, database and model download
  • Configuration — environment variables, plugin settings, Stash-Box auto-discovery
  • Plugin Usage — navigating the dashboard, identifying performers, understanding results

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Component Requirement Stash v0.25+ Docker With nvidia-container-toolkit for GPU acceleration GPU NVIDIA with 4GB+ VRAM (Recommended) — not required, CPU fallback available Disk ~2.5 GB for face recognition data, models, and working space Generated content Some features require Stash-generated content — see each feature page for prerequisites

Generated content

Performer identification requires sprite sheets (Settings > Tasks > Generate > Sprites). Scene tagger requires perceptual hashes (Settings > Tasks > Generate > Perceptual Hashes). Details are on each feature's page under "Prerequisites."

docs.title: Stash Sense Architecture
docs.text: Reference for how the system works and why key decisions were made. This page is developer-facing — for end-user docs, see the Features pages.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
Stash Sense is a two-component system: a sidecar API (Python/FastAPI) that runs face recognition and analysis, and a plugin (JS/CSS/Python) injected into the Stash web UI.

Deployment model: The sidecar runs as a Docker container alongside Stash (default port 6960). The plugin backend proxies all requests from Stash to the sidecar, bypassing browser CSP restrictions. The sidecar URL is configurable in Stash plugin settings.

Two-database design: - performers.db — Read-only, distributable. Contains performer metadata, face references, and stash-box IDs sourced from the private trainer repo. Updated via GitHub Releases. - stash_sense.db — Read-write, user-local. Contains recommendations, dismissed items, analysis watermarks, upstream snapshots, and scene fingerprints. Persists across face DB updates.

This separation means face DB updates never touch user state, and the distributable database contains no user-specific data.

Docker image: Two-stage build on nvidia/cuda:12.4.0-runtime-ubuntu22.04. ONNX models (FaceNet512 + ArcFace, ~220MB) are baked into the image. Data files (Voyager indices ~1.1GB, performers.db ~210MB) are volume-mounted from NVMe for independent updates. PyTorch, TensorFlow, and DeepFace are stripped — only needed by the trainer's offline scripts.

docs.title: Face Recognition
docs.text:
Models: RetinaFace (buffalo_sc, ONNX GPU) for detection, FaceNet512 + ArcFace for embeddings. Both embedding models use flip-averaging (original + horizontally flipped face, averaged) for more stable representations.

Pipeline (3-phase batch): 1. Extract — ffmpeg seeks N frames from scene, 8 concurrent workers 2. Detect — RetinaFace processes all frames, InsightFace norm_crop aligns faces via 5-point similarity transform 3. Embed + Match — All faces batched through both ONNX models in 2 calls (1 per model), then searched against Voyager indices (cosine space)

This replaced a per-face sequential pipeline: 53.6s → 4.8s on 1080p/60 frames/64 faces (11x speedup, embedding step 138x faster via GPU batching).

Matching: clustered_frequency_matching is the default. Faces are clustered by person using cosine distance (threshold 0.6) on concatenated FaceNet+ArcFace embeddings, then frequency-matched within each cluster. Multi-frame appearances boost confidence. Tagged-performer boost (+0.03) applied when scene already has performers tagged.

Tuned defaults (from 20-scene stratified benchmark): fusion weights 0.5/0.5 FaceNet/ArcFace, max_distance 0.5, num_frames 60, min_unique_frames 2. Baseline: ~42% scene accuracy, ~33% precision. Biggest improvement levers are num_frames and database coverage.

docs.title: Recommendations Engine
docs.text:
BaseAnalyzer pattern: Each recommendation type (duplicate scenes, missing stash-box links, upstream changes, etc.) is a pluggable analyzer with a consistent interface for running, progress tracking, and creating recommendations. The scheduler runs analyzers as background jobs.

Incremental watermarking: Most analyzers track a last_watermark timestamp or cursor and only process items modified since the last run. This keeps incremental runs fast (~seconds) versus full scans (~73 min for 7K+ performers at 5 req/s rate limit).

Polymorphic recommendations: A single recommendations table handles all entity types (duplicate_performer, duplicate_scene, unidentified_scene, missing_stashbox_link, stashbox_updates) with type-specific JSON payloads. Users review via a dashboard or contextual actions on affected pages.

docs.title: Duplicate Scene Detection
docs.text:
Stash's built-in phash matching fails with different intros/outros, trimming, aspect ratio changes, or watermarks. Stash Sense uses multi-signal detection with a confidence hierarchy.

Signal hierarchy with caps: - Stash-box ID match = 100% (authoritative) - Face fingerprint similarity = up to 85% - Metadata overlap = up to 60% - No single signal other than stash-box ID reaches 100%

Face fingerprints: Per-scene records of which performers appeared, how many times detected, and proportion of total faces. Same performers appearing in the same ratios is robust to trimming and length differences.

Diminishing returns scoring: primary + secondary × 0.3 — the second signal adds less than the first, preventing false confidence inflation.

Scalable candidate generation: Direct O(n²) comparison crashes on 15K+ scenes. Instead, a two-phase approach: 1. Candidate generation — SQL joins and inverted indices produce O(n) candidate pairs from 3 sources: stash-box ID grouping, face fingerprint self-join (shared performers), and metadata intersection (same studio AND performer). Yields 10K-50K candidates vs 112M brute-force comparisons. 2. Sequential scoring — Cursor-based pagination (id > last_id LIMIT 100) iterates candidates, scores each, writes recommendations immediately. Constant memory throughout.

docs.title: Multi-Signal Identification
docs.text:
Face recognition alone achieves ~50-60% accuracy. Additional biometric signals improve identification when faces are unclear or absent.

Late fusion architecture: Each signal is searched independently; results are combined via multiplicative scoring. Missing signals are handled gracefully (no tattoo visible → neutral multiplier).

Signals: - Face (primary) — Voyager index search, top-K candidates - Body proportions — MediaPipe pose estimation extracts shoulder-hip ratio, leg-torso ratio, arm-span-height ratio. Compared against database values with tolerance ~0.15. Returns penalty multiplier (1.0 compatible, 0.3 severe mismatch). - Tattoo presence — YOLO-based detection. Query shows tattoos but candidate has none → 0.7x penalty. Matching tattoo locations → 1.15x boost.

Fusion: final_score = face_score × body_multiplier × tattoo_multiplier

Tattoo embedding matching (semantic similarity of tattoo designs via EfficientNet-B0 1280-dim vectors) exists in the trainer but is not yet deployed to the sidecar.

docs.title: Upstream Performer Sync
docs.text:
Detects stash-box field changes and presents per-field merge controls to sync local Stash against upstream updates.

3-way diff engine: Compares upstream (current stash-box state) vs local (current Stash state) vs snapshot (last-seen upstream state stored in upstream_snapshots table). This distinguishes intentional local differences from actual upstream changes.

Merge controls: Name fields get 5 options (keep/accept/demote-to-alias/add-as-alias/custom). Aliases use union checkboxes. Simple fields use 3-option radio (keep/accept/custom). Per-field monitoring can be disabled per endpoint via upstream_field_config.

Field mapping complexity: Stash-box uses separate fields (cup_size, band_size, waist_size, hip_size, career_start_year, career_end_year) that Stash combines into compound strings (measurements "38F-24-35", career_length "2015-2023"). Translation handled in recommendations_router.py:update_performer_fields().

Dismissal model: Soft dismiss (permanent=0) resurfaces if upstream changes again. Permanent dismiss skips entirely.

docs.title: Upstream Studio & Tag Sync
docs.text:
Both follow the same BaseUpstreamAnalyzer pattern as performer sync: 3-way diff with stored snapshots, incremental watermarking, and per-field enable/disable via upstream_field_config.

Studios: Compared fields are name, URL, and parent studio. Parent studio comparison resolves the parent's stash-box ID for the current endpoint rather than comparing local numeric IDs, which would always differ from upstream UUIDs. Falls back to local ID only when the parent isn't linked to the endpoint.

Tags: Compared fields are name, description, and aliases. Tag comparison is set-based (aliases are compared as unordered sets, not ordered lists).

docs.title: Upstream Scene Sync
docs.text:
Detects changes in scene metadata, studio assignment, performer lineup, and tags between local Stash and stash-box endpoints. Uses the same BaseUpstreamAnalyzer infrastructure but with relational diffing rather than simple field comparison.

Relational diffing: Scene changes go beyond flat field comparison. Performer changes detect added/removed performers with alias detection (performer "as" credits). Tag changes are set-based (added/removed). Studio changes resolve stash-box IDs for comparison, same as the studio analyzer. Simple fields (title, date, URL, details) use standard 3-way diff.

Change detection: A scene is flagged only when at least one category has actual differences — simple field changes, a studio change, performer additions/removals/alias changes, or tag additions/removals. All entity IDs (performers, studios, tags) are resolved to stash-box IDs scoped to the current endpoint to avoid cross-endpoint mismatches.

docs.title: Logic Versioning
docs.text:
Each upstream analyzer has a logic_version class attribute (e.g., performer analyzer v2 removed the favorite field from comparison, studio analyzer v2 switched to stash-box IDs for parent studio). The version is stored in the analysis_watermarks.logic_version column.

When the version changes, the next analysis run detects the mismatch and clears all stale snapshots and watermarks for that entity type, forcing a full re-analysis. Recommendations generated under old logic that no longer produce differences are automatically resolved. This acts as a migration mechanism — when comparison logic changes (new fields, different normalization, ID resolution fixes), bumping logic_version ensures all entities are re-evaluated cleanly without manual intervention.

docs.title: Gallery & Image Identification
docs.text:
Extends face recognition from scenes (frame extraction) to gallery images (typically higher quality, better-framed).

Endpoints: /identify/image (single image) and /identify/gallery (all images in a gallery).

Aggregation: Unlike scenes, gallery images are independent — no temporal clustering needed. Results are grouped by performer across images: best distance, average distance, image count. Filtering: 2+ appearances OR single match with distance < 0.4.

Fingerprint caching: image_fingerprints and image_fingerprint_faces tables store per-image results, avoiding re-processing on subsequent requests.

docs.title: Database Self-Update
docs.text:
The sidecar checks for new face recognition database releases on GitHub and performs hot-swap updates without container restart.

Pipeline: Download → extract → verify checksums against manifest.json → swap → reload global state. Files are staged in /data/staging/, old files backed up to /data/backup/.

Availability during update: Brief 503 responses (5-10s) on /identify/* endpoints only. An update_in_progress flag gates these endpoints. Non-identification endpoints remain available.

Reload order: New DatabaseConfig → new FaceRecognizer (loads Voyager indices) → load manifest → rebuild MultiSignalMatcher → replace global references → clear flag.

Safety: Disk space check (2.5x current DB size) before download. Rollback from backup if reload fails. stash_sense.db (recommendations) is never touched during updates.

docs.title: Operation Queue
docs.text:
Persistent job queue backed by SQLite (job_queue and job_schedules tables) that manages all background analysis and maintenance work.

Job lifecycle: PENDING -> QUEUED -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED. Jobs are submitted with a type, priority, and optional cursor. The QueueManager singleton orchestrates dispatch.

Resource-aware scheduling: Each job type declares a resource requirement. Slots limit concurrency per resource type: GPU (1), CPU_HEAVY (1), NETWORK (2), LIGHT (3). A job is dispatched only when a slot is available for its resource type, preventing GPU contention or network flooding.

Priority levels: CRITICAL (0), HIGH (10), NORMAL (50), LOW (100). Lower values run first. Most analyzers default to NORMAL; database self-update uses HIGH; StashBox queries use LOW.

Incremental job support: Jobs can persist a cursor (e.g., last-processed ID or timestamp) so they resume from where they left off on subsequent runs. Combined with the watermark system, this keeps incremental analysis fast.

Schedules: job_schedules table stores cron-like schedules per job type, allowing automatic periodic runs without external schedulers.

docs.title: Resource Management
docs.text:
ResourceManager handles lazy loading and idle unloading of heavy resources to free GPU memory and RAM when not in use.

Resources managed: Face recognition data (Voyager indices + metadata), tattoo detection models, body proportion indices. Each is registered with a loader and unloader function.

Lifecycle: Resources are loaded on first require() call and cached. A background task periodically calls check_idle(). Resources unused for 1800 seconds (30 minutes) are unloaded — their unloader runs, data references are cleared, and gc.collect() reclaims memory. Thread-safe via internal locking.

docs.title: Model Management
docs.text:
Optional ONNX models (tattoo detection) are not baked into the Docker image. They are downloaded on-demand from GitHub Releases.

Download pipeline: ModelManager tracks each model's expected SHA256 hash. Downloads are triggered via the /models/download/{model_name} endpoint, run in the background, and validated against the hash before being placed in the models directory. The /models/status endpoint reports per-model installation state.

Capabilities API: The /capabilities endpoint inspects which data files and model files are present on disk and reports which features are available (upstream sync, duplicate detection, identification, tattoo signal). The plugin UI uses this to show/hide feature-specific controls and offer model download prompts for missing capabilities.

docs.title: Plugin Distribution
docs.text:
The plugin is distributed via a Stash-compatible package index hosted on GitHub Pages.

Build: build_plugin_index.sh extracts metadata from plugin/stash-sense.yml, creates a zip of the plugin directory, generates an index.yml with version info (plugin version + git commit hash), and writes both to an output directory.

Deployment: A GitHub Actions docs workflow triggers on version tag pushes and plugin file changes. It runs the build script and deploys the output to the gh-pages branch via ghp-import. The resulting index is available at https://carrotwaxr.github.io/stash-sense/plugin/index.yml.

Usage: Users add this URL as a plugin source in Stash settings (Settings > Plugins > Available Plugins). Stash checks the index for updates and installs/updates the plugin automatically.

docs.title: Essential Configuration
docs.text: Two things must be configured for Stash Sense to work:

docs.title: 1. Sidecar Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set these when starting the Docker container:

Variable Required Description STASH_URL Yes URL to your Stash instance (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:9999) STASH_API_KEY Yes Stash API key from Settings > Security > API Key STASH_SENSE_API_KEY No Key that external tools such as stash-curator send in the ApiKey header to use the driver API. When it is empty, the driver API is open to your network. 
-e STASH_URL=http://your-stash-host:9999 \
-e STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key

docs.title: 2. Plugin Sidecar URL
docs.text:
In Stash, go to Settings > Plugins > Stash Sense and set the Sidecar URL to the address of your Stash Sense container (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:6960).

This tells the plugin backend where to forward requests. The right URL depends on your setup — see Networking below.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
The sidecar runs inside a Docker container, so localhost means different things depending on where you are. Here's what to use for STASH_URL (sidecar connecting to Stash) and the Sidecar URL plugin setting (Stash connecting to sidecar):

Your Setup STASH_URL Sidecar URL Same machine, both in Docker (shared network) Container name (e.g., http://stash:9999) Container name (e.g., http://stash-sense:5000) Same machine, both in Docker (no shared network) Host LAN IP (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:9999) Host LAN IP (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:6960) Same machine, Stash runs natively (not in Docker) http://host.docker.internal:9999 http://127.0.0.1:6960 Different machines Stash machine's LAN IP Sidecar machine's LAN IP

Key points:

  • Don't use localhost in STASH_URL — inside the container, localhost refers to the container itself, not the host machine.
  • host.docker.internal resolves to the host machine's IP from inside a container. This is how the sidecar reaches Stash when Stash runs natively on the host (e.g., as a Windows binary). It works automatically on Docker Desktop (Windows/Mac). On Linux, add --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway to your docker run command.
  • Use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost for the Sidecar URL when Stash runs natively. On Windows, localhost can resolve to ::1 (IPv6) on recent Docker Desktop versions, causing "connection refused" errors. Using 127.0.0.1 explicitly avoids this.
  • When both are in Docker on separate networks, use the host's LAN IP for both. Docker container names only resolve on shared Docker networks.

docs.title: Stash-Box Endpoints
docs.text:
Stash-Box endpoint credentials are not configured as environment variables. The sidecar auto-discovers all configured Stash-Box endpoints from your Stash instance's Settings > Metadata Providers at startup.

Any endpoints you've added there (StashDB, FansDB, ThePornDB, etc.) are automatically available for upstream sync and scene tagging.

To add a new endpoint, configure it in Stash's Metadata Providers settings, then restart the sidecar or use the Refresh button in the plugin's Settings tab.

docs.title: Runtime Settings
docs.text:
Most performance and recognition settings are configured via the plugin's Settings tab rather than environment variables. The sidecar auto-detects your hardware and sets sensible defaults.

Settings you can adjust include:

  • Frames per scene — How many frames to sample for face recognition
  • Embedding batch size — Faces processed per GPU call
  • Rate limits — Requests/second to local Stash API
  • Signal toggles — Enable/disable body proportion and tattoo detection signals

See Settings Reference for the full list of adjustable options.

docs.title: Volume Mounts
docs.text:
Container Path Purpose Mode /data Database files, models, and local data (stash_sense.db) Read-write /root/.insightface Cached face detection model weights (~500 MB) Read-write /media Your media library, the same files Stash reads Read-only (read-write only for features that write files)

Warning

The /data volume must be read-write. The sidecar writes stash_sense.db (recommendations, settings, analysis history) here, and in-app database updates download files to this directory.

docs.title: Media library
docs.text:
Features that read video files directly (audio fingerprints, frame sampling) and features that write next to them (subtitles) need the library mounted into the container. Mount it read-only unless you turn on a feature that writes files. Those features check the mount and refuse to run with a message naming the fix when it is read-only.

Stash and the sidecar usually see the library at different paths. MEDIA_PATH_MAP maps Stash's paths to the sidecar's:

Stash sees Sidecar mount MEDIA_PATH_MAP /data/Studio/a.mp4 /media /data=/media /data and /archive /media, /media2 /data=/media,/archive=/media2

Without a map, Stash's paths are used unchanged, which works when you mount the library at the same container path Stash uses. The plugin's Settings tab and GET /health report each mount and whether it is rw, ro or missing.

docs.title: File ownership (PUID / PGID)
docs.text:
The container starts as root, hands /data and the InsightFace cache to PUID:PGID, then drops to that user. Everything the sidecar creates (database, models, subtitles) is owned by PUID:PGID. The defaults, 99:100, match unRAID's nobody:users. On other hosts use the owner of your library (id -u, id -g). PUID=0 keeps the old run-as-root behaviour. UMASK (default 022) sets the file mode mask.

The media library is never chowned. In read-write mode PUID:PGID needs write permission on the folders it writes into.

docs.title: CPU and GPU
docs.text:
CPU-heavy jobs run ffmpeg under nice with an optional thread cap, both set in Settings > Performance (media_job_nice, media_job_threads). To keep the whole container off some cores, add --cpuset-cpus=2-7 (your core list) to the template's Extra Parameters or cpuset: "2-7" in compose.

The GPU tier comes from the card's VRAM, read through NVML (bundled in the image) or nvidia-smi. Both need the NVIDIA runtime (--runtime=nvidia, or the compose deploy.resources block). Without it, the sidecar reports No GPU and uses the CPU tier.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
The sidecar listens on port 5000 inside the container. The recommended host port is 6960:

-p 6960:5000

docs.title: Database Files
docs.text:
The /data volume should contain the files from a stash-sense-data release:

/data/
├── performers.db        # Performer metadata (SQLite)
├── face_facenet.voy     # FaceNet512 embedding index
├── face_arcface.voy     # ArcFace embedding index
├── faces.json           # Face-to-performer mapping
├── performers.json      # Performer lookup data
├── manifest.json        # Version and checksums
├── models/              # (auto-created) ONNX models downloaded via Settings UI
│   ├── facenet512.onnx  # FaceNet512 embedding model (~90 MB)
│   └── arcface.onnx     # ArcFace embedding model (~130 MB)
└── stash_sense.db       # (auto-created) Your local data — do not delete

Note

stash_sense.db and the models/ directory are created automatically by the sidecar. They are not part of the database release and should not be deleted during updates. Both the database and models can be downloaded from the plugin's Settings tab after startup.

docs.title: Environment Variable Migration
docs.text:
The following environment variables have been replaced by runtime settings. If detected at startup, they are automatically migrated to the settings database:

Old Variable New Setting STASH_RATE_LIMIT stash_api_rate ENABLE_BODY_SIGNAL body_signal_enabled ENABLE_TATTOO_SIGNAL tattoo_signal_enabled FACE_CANDIDATES face_candidates

Environment variables that remain (connection strings):

  • STASH_URL, STASH_API_KEY, DATA_DIR, LOG_LEVEL
  • MEDIA_PATH_MAP, MEDIA_DIR (default /media), PUID, PGID, UMASK

docs.title: Configuration Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] STASH_URL and STASH_API_KEY set as container environment variables
  • [ ] Sidecar URL configured in Stash plugin settings
  • [ ] Stash-Box endpoints configured in Stash's Settings > Metadata Providers (for upstream sync and scene tagging)
  • [ ] /data volume mounted read-write
  • [ ] /root/.insightface volume mounted (prevents re-downloading detection model on restart)
  • [ ] Media library mounted at /media (read-only) and MEDIA_PATH_MAP set if Stash uses a different path
  • [ ] PUID / PGID match the owner of your library

docs.title: Where the Data Comes From
docs.text:
The face recognition database is built and published in the stash-sense-data repository. It contains performer metadata and face embeddings sourced from multiple Stash-Box endpoints:

Source Type Performers StashDB Primary ~100,000+ FansDB Supplementary Varies ThePornDB Supplementary ~10,000 PMVStash Supplementary ~6,500 JAVStash Supplementary ~21,700

Additional sources include Babepedia, Freeones, IAFD, and other public performer databases via hybrid scraping.

Current stats (v2026.02.18): 108,001 performers, 366,794 face embeddings.

The database is built using a private training pipeline that:

  1. Downloads performer images from each source
  2. Detects and aligns faces using RetinaFace with 5-point similarity transform
  3. Generates embeddings using FaceNet512 and ArcFace models with flip-averaging
  4. Builds Voyager vector indices for fast cosine-distance search

Database releases are published as zip files on the stash-sense-data releases page.

docs.title: Database Files
docs.text:
The data directory contains:

File Size Purpose performers.db ~210 MB SQLite database with performer metadata and Stash-Box IDs face_facenet.voy ~550 MB FaceNet512 embedding Voyager index face_arcface.voy ~550 MB ArcFace embedding Voyager index faces.json ~15 MB Face-to-performer mapping performers.json ~10 MB Performer lookup data manifest.json <1 KB Version, checksums, and build metadata

docs.title: Two-Database Design
docs.text:
Stash Sense uses two separate databases:

  • performers.db + Voyager indices — The distributable face recognition data. Updated via stash-sense-data releases either in-app (Settings tab) or manually. Contains no user-specific information.
  • stash_sense.db (read-write, user-local) — Your recommendation history, dismissed items, analysis watermarks, upstream snapshots, scene fingerprints, operation queue, and settings overrides.

This separation means database updates never touch your personal data, and the distributable database contains nothing specific to your library.

docs.title: Via the Plugin UI
docs.text:
1. Open the Settings tab in the Stash Sense dashboard
  2. The Database section shows your current version and checks for updates automatically
  3. If an update is available, click Update
  4. Progress is shown in real-time (download, extract, verify, swap, reload)

docs.title: Via the API
docs.text:
Check for updates:

curl http://localhost:6960/database/check-update

{
  "current_version": "2026.02.12",
  "latest_version": "2026.02.18",
  "update_available": true,
  "release_name": "Database Release v2026.02.18",
  "download_size_mb": 1478,
  "published_at": "2026-02-18T01:09:34Z"
}

Start an update:

curl -X POST http://localhost:6960/database/update

Check update progress:

curl http://localhost:6960/database/update/status

docs.title: Manual Database Update
docs.text:
If you prefer to update manually (e.g., on a system without internet access):

  1. Download the latest release zip from stash-sense-data releases
  2. Stop the container: docker stop stash-sense
  3. Extract the zip into your data directory, replacing existing files
  4. Start the container: docker start stash-sense

The stash_sense.db file in your data directory is your personal data — do not delete it during a manual update.

docs.title: Update Safety
docs.text:
• A timestamped backup is created before every update
  • SHA-256 checksums are verified against manifest.json
  • On failure, the sidecar automatically rolls back to the backup
  • Face identification endpoints return 503 briefly during the swap (~5-10 seconds)
  • All other API endpoints remain available during updates
  • stash_sense.db (your recommendations, settings, history) is never touched

docs.title: Driver API v1
docs.text:
The driver API is the stable surface external tools use to drive stash-sense. Its first user is the stash-curator CLI (sense commands). Everything else the sidecar serves (/queue, /review, /recommendations and the rest) is internal to the plugin and changes without notice. Tools must only call the endpoints on this page.

  • Base path: /api/v1/driver
  • Versioning: shapes on this page don't change within v1. New optional request fields and new response keys may be added. Removing or renaming a field, changing its type or meaning, or tightening validation goes to /api/v2.
  • Contract tests: api/tests/test_driver_api.py pins every request and response shape. A failing contract test means a breaking change.
  • Direction: tools call stash-sense, and stash-sense never calls them.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Set STASH_SENSE_API_KEY in the sidecar's environment. Every driver call must then send it in the ApiKey header, the same header Stash uses:

ApiKey: <STASH_SENSE_API_KEY>

A missing or wrong key gets 401 unauthorized, checked before the request body is read. When the variable is unset, the driver API is open; GET /api/v1/driver reports auth_required: false. The key protects only the driver routes. The plugin's internal routes stay open on the LAN, as before.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC, e.g. 2026-11-17T10:00:00Z.
  • Ids are integers, except Stash ids (scenes, files, performers), which are strings.
  • Every error response has the same body. code is stable and meant for branching; message is for people. Some codes add fields:
{"error": {"code": "stale", "message": "The library changed since this preview; review the updated plan", "preview": {...}}}
  • A body that doesn't match the schema, including unknown fields, gets 422 invalid_request with fields listing the problems.
  • Recommendations of types marked unfinished are hidden unless the user turns on Settings > Features > Show Unfinished Features. Hidden types are left out of lists, and naming one directly gets 403 hidden_type.
  • Recommendations that name a scene on the user's exclusion list (Settings > Curation) are left out of lists. Naming one directly gets 403 scene_excluded with scene_ids. When Stash can't be read to check the list, the call fails closed with 503 exclusion_unavailable.

docs.title: GET /api/v1/driver
docs.text:
{
  "api_version": 1,
  "sidecar_version": "0.1.3-beta.3",
  "auth_required": true,
  "job_types": [
    {"type": "duplicate_performer", "name": "Duplicate Performer Detection",
     "description": "Finds performers that may be duplicates", "default_priority": 50, "params": {}}
  ],
  "review_types": [
    {"type": "review_demo", "name": "Review Demo", "description": "..."}
  ]
}

job_types lists the jobs a caller may start. review_types lists the recommendation types that can be previewed and accepted. params describes the parameters a job type takes; no type takes any yet.

docs.title: POST /jobs
docs.text:
{"type": "duplicate_performer", "priority": "high", "params": {}}
  • priority (optional) is "critical", "high", "normal", "low" or the matching number (0, 10, 50, 100; lower runs first). Other values get 422. It defaults to the type's default_priority.
  • params (optional) must be empty or omitted until a job type declares params.

Only one job per type is queued or running at a time.

  • 201 returns {"created": true, "job": <Job>}.
  • 200 returns {"created": false, "job": <Job>} when a job of that type is already queued or running; job is that existing job.
  • Errors: 404 unknown_job_type, 403 hidden_type, 400 invalid_params, 409 media_not_writable (the job writes media and the media mount is read-only).

docs.title: GET /jobs/{id}
docs.text:
Returns {"job": <Job>}, or 404 not_found.

{
  "id": 12,
  "type": "duplicate_performer",
  "status": "completed",
  "priority": 10,
  "progress": {"processed": 11, "total": 11},
  "error": null,
  "result": {"analysis_run_id": 4, "items_processed": 11, "recommendations_created": 2, "excluded_skipped": 0},
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T10:00:00Z",
  "started_at": "2026-11-17T10:00:01Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-11-17T10:00:03Z"
}

status is one of queued, running, stopping, completed, failed or cancelled. progress.total is null until the job knows its total. result is null until the job finishes, and stays null for job types that don't report one. Analysis jobs report the shape above. error holds the failure message when status is failed.

Typical loop: POST /jobs, then poll GET /jobs/{id} every few seconds until status is completed, failed or cancelled. After that, read the new recommendations from the feed.

docs.title: The Recommendation object
docs.text:
{
  "id": 41,
  "type": "review_demo",
  "status": "pending",
  "target_type": "scene",
  "target_id": "1234",
  "confidence": 1.0,
  "evidence": {"tag": "stash-sense-review-demo"},
  "reviewable": true,
  "resolution": null,
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T10:00:03Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-17T10:00:03Z"
}
  • status is pending, dismissed or resolved.
  • evidence is the full payload the analyzer recorded. Its shape depends on the type.
  • reviewable is true when the type can be previewed and accepted through this API (it is listed in review_types). Other types can be read and dismissed only.
  • resolution is set when status is resolved: {"action": "applied", "details": {"apply_log_id": 7, "option": {...}}, "resolved_at": "..."}.

docs.title: GET /recommendations?type=&status=&since=&cursor=&limit=
docs.text:
Returns recommendations in the order they last changed (updated_at, then id), oldest first.

{"recommendations": [<Recommendation>, ...], "next_cursor": "MjAyNi0x...", "has_more": true}
  • since: an ISO 8601 time. Only recommendations updated at or after it are returned. A time without an offset is read as UTC.
  • cursor: the next_cursor from an earlier call. Only rows after that one are returned.
  • limit: 1 to 500, default 100.
  • has_more is true when the page is full, so call again with next_cursor.

The list doubles as a change feed. Every status change (accept, dismiss, revert) and every re-analysis moves a recommendation's updated_at forward. Keep the last next_cursor and call again later to receive only what changed since. One recommendation may come back more than once across calls, once per change, so key on id.

Rows from the current and previous second are held back, so a change shows up within about two seconds. updated_at has one-second resolution and is stamped when a write runs, not when it commits; the hold-back keeps a cursor from pointing into a second that can still gain rows behind it.

The feed reports changes, not deletions. duplicate_scenes (unfinished) drops its pending recommendations on each run and recreates them with new ids. Treat a 404 on a recommendation you hold as "gone", and re-read a recommendation before acting on it.

Errors: 400 invalid_since, 400 invalid_cursor.

docs.title: GET /recommendations/{id}
docs.text:
{"recommendation": <Recommendation>, "preview": <Preview> | null, "preview_error": {"code": "not_found", "message": "..."} | null}

For a pending, reviewable recommendation, preview is the plan accepting it would apply now, with the suggested option. Otherwise it is null. When the plan can't be built (for example, the scene is gone from Stash), preview is null and preview_error carries the error's code and message; the recommendation itself is still returned, so it can be dismissed. Errors: 404 not_found, 403 hidden_type, 403 scene_excluded.

docs.title: POST /recommendations/{id}/preview
docs.text:
{"option": {"keep_file_id": "88"}}

Returns {"preview": <Preview>} for the chosen option. A partial option is filled in from the suggestion, and an empty body previews the suggestion. Errors: 409 not_reviewable, 422 rejected (the option is not one the type offers, e.g. a file that isn't on the scene), 404 not_found (the target is gone from Stash).

docs.title: The Preview object
docs.text:
{
  "revision": "4f2a9c0d1e3b5a7c9d0e1f2a",
  "summary": "rename, delete 1 file(s)",
  "option": {"keep_file_id": "88", "title": "clip"},
  "default_option": {"keep_file_id": "88", "title": "clip"},
  "is_default_option": true,
  "high_confidence": true,
  "choices": [
    {"field": "keep_file_id", "label": "File to keep", "kind": "pick",
     "values": [{"value": "87", "label": "clip-a.mp4"}, {"value": "88", "label": "clip.mp4"}]},
    {"field": "title", "label": "Title", "kind": "text"}
  ],
  "evidence": {"scene": {"id": "1234", "title": ""}, "files": [...]},
  "plan": {
    "field_changes": [
      {"entity_type": "scene", "entity_id": "1234", "field": "title", "before": "", "after": "clip"}
    ],
    "keep_files": [
      {"file_id": "88", "scene_id": "1234", "path": "/media/x/clip.mp4", "size": 200,
       "fingerprints": {"oshash": "...", "phash": "..."}}
    ],
    "delete_files": [
      {"file_id": "87", "scene_id": "1234", "path": "/media/x/clip-a.mp4", "size": 100, "fingerprints": {...}}
    ],
    "primary_file": {"scene_id": "1234", "before": "87", "after": "88"},
    "bytes_reclaimed": 100
  },
  "trash_path": "/data/.trash"
}
  • revision fingerprints exactly what this plan would do: the option, every field's before and after, and every kept and deleted file. It belongs to this option. A different option, or any library change that alters the plan, gives a different revision.
  • plan is the complete outcome of an accept. primary_file is set when the scene's primary file moves to a kept file before the others are deleted.
  • trash_path is where deleted files go. An empty string means they are deleted permanently, because Stash has no trash configured.
  • choices are the inputs a caller may set in option. A pick lists its values; a text takes any string.
  • high_confidence means the type would batch-accept this suggestion without a person looking at it.

docs.title: POST /recommendations/{id}/accept
docs.text:
{"option": {"keep_file_id": "88", "title": "clip"}, "revision": "4f2a9c0d1e3b5a7c9d0e1f2a", "confirm_delete": ["87"]}

The sidecar rebuilds the plan from Stash's current state with option and applies it only if its revision equals revision. The caller therefore applies exactly the plan it showed.

  • confirm_delete must list exactly the file_ids in plan.delete_files. Leave it empty when nothing is deleted.
  • 200 returns {"already_applied": false, "entry": <ApplyLogEntry>, "warnings": []}.
  • Idempotent: accepting a recommendation that was already applied returns 200 with already_applied: true and the original entry, and writes nothing. That holds even when the second call carries an old revision.
  • warnings lists bookkeeping that failed after the writes succeeded, e.g. marking the recommendation resolved. The writes still happened.

Errors:

Status code Meaning Extra fields 409 stale The plan for this option no longer matches revision. Nothing was written. preview: the fresh Preview 409 confirm_delete confirm_delete doesn't name exactly the files the plan deletes. files (file_id, path, size), bytes 409 not_pending The recommendation is dismissed, or was resolved some other way. 409 not_reviewable The type can't be accepted through this API. 422 rejected The option is invalid, or the plan breaks a safety rule (e.g. it would delete every file of a scene). Nothing was written. 502 apply_failed A Stash write failed part way. entry: the apply log entry recording which steps ran 403 scene_excluded The recommendation or its plan touches an excluded scene. scene_ids

docs.title: POST /recommendations/{id}/dismiss
docs.text:
{"reason": "not a duplicate", "permanent": false}

Both fields are optional. A dismissed target is not recommended again by later runs; with permanent: true that also holds after its data changes. Returns {"recommendation": <Recommendation>}. Dismissing an already dismissed recommendation is a no-op. A resolved one gets 409 not_pending, and one naming an excluded scene gets 403 scene_excluded.

docs.title: POST /recommendations/{id}/split-result
docs.text:
{"status": "applied", "cut_scene_ids": ["501", "502"], "strategy": "reencode", "message": ""}

For a review plan that hands a split to an external tool. Accepting such a plan writes nothing to Stash: the accepted recommendation's resolution.details carries the split for the tool to execute, and the tool reports back here.

resolution.details.split, when present:

{"scene_id": "7", "file_id": "70", "oshash": "abc", "size": 1000, "duration": 3000.0,
 "ranges": [{"start": 0.0, "end": 1500.0}, {"start": 1500.0, "end": 3000.0}],
 "cuts": [1500.0]}

ranges has one entry per output scene, in seconds of the file, contiguous except where the start or end is trimmed. split: null (or no split key) means the scene is to be left whole, and there is nothing to execute or report.

Body: status is applied or failed (required); cut_scene_ids (the scenes the tool created, default []), strategy and message (default "") are optional, and unknown fields are refused with 422 invalid_request.

Returns {"recommendation": <Recommendation>}. The body is stored at resolution.details.split_result together with reported_at (UTC, ISO 8601), the recommendation's updated_at moves forward so the change feed shows it, and the apply log gets an entry with action: "split_result" whose result.accept_log_id is the accept's entry. Reporting the same result again returns 200 and writes nothing; a different result replaces the stored one and is logged again. status, resolution.action and resolved_at do not change.

Errors: 404 not_found, 403 hidden_type, 403 scene_excluded, 409 not_accepted (the recommendation is not resolved), 409 no_split (resolved without details.split).

docs.title: Apply log
docs.text: Every accept is logged before its first write, with the plan, the state it replaced, and each step that ran. The log is an audit record: unlike the recommendation list, it is not filtered by hidden types or the exclusion list.

docs.title: GET /apply-log?since=&type=&limit=
docs.text:
{"entries": [<ApplyLogEntry>, ...], "next_since": 9, "has_more": false}

Entries are returned oldest first. Pass the last id you saw as since to get only newer ones; next_since is the id to pass next time. type filters by recommendation type, and limit is 1 to 500 (default 100).

docs.title: GET /apply-log/{id}
docs.text: Returns {"entry": <ApplyLogEntry>}, or 404 not_found.

docs.title: The ApplyLogEntry object
docs.text:
{
  "id": 9,
  "action": "apply",
  "status": "applied",
  "rec_id": 41,
  "rec_type": "review_demo",
  "target_type": "scene",
  "target_id": "1234",
  "batch_id": null,
  "reverts_id": null,
  "reverted_by": null,
  "option": {"keep_file_id": "88", "title": "clip"},
  "revision": "4f2a9c0d1e3b5a7c9d0e1f2a",
  "plan": {<same shape as Preview.plan>},
  "result": {"steps": [...], "bytes_reclaimed": 100, "files_deleted": 1, "fields_changed": 1},
  "error": null,
  "trash_path": "/data/.trash",
  "created_at": "2026-11-17T10:05:00Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-11-17T10:05:01Z"
}
  • action is apply, revert for an undo made in the Stash UI, or split_result for a result an external tool reported for an accepted split. On a revert, reverts_id names the entry it undid, and that entry's reverted_by points back.
  • status is applying, applied or failed. An applying entry is still in flight; re-read it with GET /apply-log/{id}. Because the feed moves by id, it won't return that entry again.
  • batch_id groups entries that a batch accept in the Stash UI applied together.

docs.title: Example: curator session
docs.text:
B=http://10.0.0.5:5000/api/v1/driver; H="ApiKey: $STASH_SENSE_API_KEY"

# Start a job and wait for it
curl -s -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"type":"duplicate_performer"}' $B/jobs
curl -s -H "$H" $B/jobs/12

# Read what's pending, then keep next_cursor for the next session
curl -s -H "$H" "$B/recommendations?status=pending&limit=50"

# Show one, then apply exactly what was shown
curl -s -H "$H" $B/recommendations/41
curl -s -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"option":{"keep_file_id":"88","title":"clip"},"revision":"4f2a9c0d1e3b5a7c9d0e1f2a","confirm_delete":["87"]}' \
  $B/recommendations/41/accept

# What was applied since last time
curl -s -H "$H" "$B/apply-log?since=8"

docs.title: Step 1: Start the Container
docs.text: For best performance, install Stash Sense on the same machine as Stash.

docs.title: GPU vs CPU
docs.text:
Stash Sense uses GPU acceleration for face detection and embedding inference. An NVIDIA GPU with 4GB+ VRAM is recommended but not required — CPU mode works, just slower (~2-3 seconds per frame vs ~200ms with GPU).

  • GPU mode requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed on the host
  • CPU mode requires no additional setup — just omit the GPU flags

docs.title: Docker Run
docs.text:
With GPU (recommended):

docker run -d \
  --name stash-sense \
  --gpus all \
  -p 6960:5000 \
  -e STASH_URL=http://your-stash-host:9999 \
  -e STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key \
  -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 \
  -e MEDIA_PATH_MAP=/data=/media \
  -v /path/to/stash-sense-data:/data \
  -v stash-sense-insightface:/root/.insightface \
  -v /path/to/your/library:/media:ro \
  carrotwaxr/stash-sense:latest

CPU only — remove --gpus all:

docker run -d \
  --name stash-sense \
  -p 6960:5000 \
  -e STASH_URL=http://your-stash-host:9999 \
  -e STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key \
  -e PUID=1000 -e PGID=1000 \
  -e MEDIA_PATH_MAP=/data=/media \
  -v /path/to/stash-sense-data:/data \
  -v stash-sense-insightface:/root/.insightface \
  -v /path/to/your/library:/media:ro \
  carrotwaxr/stash-sense:latest

PUID/PGID should be the owner of your library (id -u, id -g); unRAID uses 99/100. MEDIA_PATH_MAP maps the path Stash reports for a file to the path inside this container. See Configuration for both.

The /data volume must be read-write

The sidecar writes stash_sense.db (your recommendations, settings, and analysis history) to /data, and in-app database updates also write here. Do not mount with :ro.

Docker Compose

Create a docker-compose.yml:

services:
  stash-sense:
    image: carrotwaxr/stash-sense:latest
    container_name: stash-sense
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6960:5000"
    volumes:
      - /path/to/stash-sense-data:/data
      - stash-sense-insightface:/root/.insightface
      - /path/to/your/library:/media:ro
    environment:
      - STASH_URL=http://your-stash-host:9999
      - STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - MEDIA_PATH_MAP=/data=/media
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu]

volumes:
  stash-sense-insightface:

For CPU only, remove the deploy.resources block.

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Step 2: Verify
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:6960/health

Should return:

{
  "status": "degraded",
  "database_loaded": false,
  "performer_count": 0,
  "face_count": 0
}

This is expected — the database and models haven't been downloaded yet. Once downloaded (Step 4), the status will change to "healthy".

docs.title: Step 3: Install the Stash Plugin
docs.text:
Add the Stash Sense plugin source in Stash:

  1. Go to Settings > Plugins > Available Plugins
  2. Click Add Source and enter:
  3. Name: Stash Sense
  4. URL: https://carrotwaxr.github.io/stash-sense/plugin/index.yml
  5. Click Save
  6. Find Stash Sense in the available plugins list and click Install
  7. Go to Settings > Plugins > Stash Sense and set the Sidecar URL to http://your-stash-sense-host:6960

Tip

If Stash and Stash Sense run on the same machine, use the host IP (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:6960). Docker container names don't resolve unless both containers share a Docker network.

docs.title: Step 4: Download Database and Models
docs.text: Click Stash Sense in Stash's top navigation bar (or go to /plugins/stash-sense) to open the Stash Sense dashboard, then go to the Settings tab.

docs.title: Download the Face Recognition Database
docs.text:
1. In the Database section, click Update to download the latest database (~1.5 GB)
  2. Progress is shown in real-time (download, extract, verify, swap)
  3. Once complete, the /health endpoint will report "database_loaded": true

docs.title: Download ONNX Models
docs.text:
1. In the Models section, click Download All to download the required face recognition models (~220 MB)
  2. Two models are required: FaceNet512 (~90 MB) and ArcFace (~130 MB)
  3. Optional models (tattoo detection) can be downloaded separately if needed

Face recognition won't work until both the database and models are downloaded

If you try to identify performers before downloading, you'll see a "Database not loaded" or model-not-found error.

Manual database download

If you prefer to pre-populate the data directory before starting the container:

  1. Download the latest release from stash-sense-data
  2. Extract the zip into your data directory (the path mounted to /data)
  3. The sidecar will detect the files on startup

docs.title: unRAID
docs.text: See unRAID Setup for template-based installation and GPU passthrough configuration.

docs.title: Windows / WSL
docs.text:
Stash Sense runs on Windows via Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend.

Setup:

  • Ensure WSL 2 is enabled (Docker Desktop > Settings > General > Use the WSL 2 based engine)
  • For GPU support, install the NVIDIA CUDA on WSL driver and enable GPU support in Docker Desktop (Settings > Resources > WSL Integration)

Multi-line commands: PowerShell uses backtick (`) instead of backslash (\) for line continuation:

docker run -d `
  --name stash-sense `
  --gpus all `
  -p 6960:5000 `
  -e STASH_URL=http://your-stash-host:9999 `
  -e STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key `
  -v C:/Users/you/stash-sense-data:/data `
  -v stash-sense-insightface:/root/.insightface `
  carrotwaxr/stash-sense:latest

Networking gotchas:

  • On recent Docker Desktop versions, localhost may resolve to ::1 (IPv6) instead of 127.0.0.1. If curl http://localhost:6960/health fails with "connection refused," try http://127.0.0.1:6960/health instead.
  • When setting STASH_URL, use your machine's LAN IP (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:9999) rather than localhost, since the container has its own network namespace.
  • Similarly, set the plugin's Sidecar URL to the LAN IP (e.g., http://192.168.1.100:6960), not localhost.

Volume performance: Named volumes (e.g., stash-sense-data:/data) are faster than bind mounts to Windows paths. If you use bind mounts, paths on the WSL filesystem are faster than Windows-mounted paths (/mnt/c/... is slower due to WSL2's 9P filesystem bridge).

docs.title: Installation Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Sidecar container running (docker ps shows stash-sense)
  • [ ] Health check returns a response (curl http://localhost:6960/health)
  • [ ] Plugin installed in Stash (visible in Settings > Plugins)
  • [ ] Sidecar URL configured in plugin settings
  • [ ] Face recognition database downloaded (Settings tab > Database > Update)
  • [ ] ONNX models downloaded (Settings tab > Models > Download All)

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Configuration — environment variables, Stash-Box auto-discovery, runtime settings
  • Plugin Usage — navigating the dashboard, identifying performers
  • Features — start with performer identification

docs.title: 1. Add the plugin source
docs.text:
In Stash, go to Settings > Plugins > Available Plugins and click Add Source:

  • Name: Stash Sense
  • URL: https://carrotwaxr.github.io/stash-sense/plugin/index.yml

docs.title: 2. Install the plugin
docs.text: Find Stash Sense in the available plugins list and click Install.

docs.title: 3. Configure the sidecar URL
docs.text: Go to Settings > Plugins > Stash Sense and set the Sidecar URL to the address of your Stash Sense container (e.g., http://10.0.0.4:6960).

docs.title: 4. Open the dashboard
docs.text: Click Stash Sense in Stash's top navigation bar, or go to /plugins/stash-sense, to open the Stash Sense dashboard.

docs.title: Identifying Performers in a Scene
docs.text:
1. Navigate to a scene page in Stash
  2. Click the "Identify Performers" button
  3. Wait for analysis (uses the scene's sprite sheet)
  4. Review results in the modal:
  5. Detected face thumbnails grouped by person
  6. Best match from the performer database
  7. Distance score (lower is better)
  8. Click "Add to Scene" to link the performer

See Performer Identification for details on how matching works and how to interpret results.

docs.title: Recommendations Dashboard
docs.text:
The main dashboard is accessible at /plugins/stash-sense in your Stash UI. It shows all actionable recommendations:

  • Upstream Changes — Field updates detected from Stash-Box endpoints, with 3-way diff views
  • Duplicates — Candidate duplicate scenes with confidence scores
  • All Recommendations — Combined view with filtering and bulk actions

Each recommendation type runs as a background analyzer with incremental watermarking — only items modified since the last run are re-processed.

docs.title: Settings Tab
docs.text:
The Settings tab in the dashboard provides:

  • Database — Current version, check for updates, download/update
  • Models — Download or remove ONNX models
  • Stash-Box Endpoints — View auto-discovered endpoints, enable/disable for upstream sync, refresh
  • Hardware — Current tier and setting overrides
  • Runtime Settings — Adjust performance, recognition, and signal settings

See Settings Reference for the full list of adjustable options.

docs.title: Operation Queue
docs.text:
The Operations tab shows:

  • Job Status — Real-time status of running, queued, completed, and failed jobs with progress indicators
  • Manual Triggers — Start analysis runs, upstream sync, scene tagging, and other operations on demand
  • Scheduling — Configure recurring analysis jobs with interval and enable/disable controls

Jobs run in the background with resource-aware scheduling — GPU-intensive work won't overlap with other GPU jobs, and network-bound operations respect rate limits.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Scene must have a sprite sheet generated for performer identification
  • Stash Sense sidecar must be running and accessible

docs.title: Generating Sprite Sheets
docs.text:
If a scene doesn't have sprites:

  1. Go to the scene page
  2. Click Generate > Enable Sprite
  3. Or bulk generate: Settings > Tasks > Generate > Sprites

docs.title: "Failed to connect to Stash Sense"
docs.text:
• Verify sidecar is running: curl http://your-host:6960/health
  • Check Sidecar URL in plugin settings matches your container's host and port
  • If using Docker, ensure network connectivity between Stash and the sidecar

docs.title: "No faces detected"
docs.text:
• Scene may not have clear face shots
  • Sprite sheet may be low quality or missing
  • Try a different scene to verify setup

docs.title: Plugin not appearing
docs.text:
1. Check plugin files are in the correct location
  2. Reload plugins in Stash settings
  3. Check Stash logs for errors

docs.title: Settings System
docs.text: The sidecar includes a hardware-adaptive settings system that auto-detects your hardware at startup and picks optimal defaults. All runtime settings can be viewed and adjusted via the Settings API or the Plugin Settings UI.

docs.title: Hardware Detection
docs.text: On startup, the sidecar probes: - GPU: ONNX Runtime CUDA provider + pynvml for VRAM/model name - CPU: Core count (respects Docker cgroup limits) - Memory: Total and available RAM (respects Docker cgroup limits) - Storage: Free disk space at the data directory

docs.title: Hardware Tiers
docs.text:
Based on detection results, the sidecar classifies your hardware into a tier:

Tier Criteria Batch Size Concurrency Detection Res Frames/Scene gpu-high CUDA + VRAM >= 4GB 32 8 640px 60 gpu-low CUDA + VRAM < 4GB 16 6 640px 60 cpu No CUDA 4 2 320px 30

docs.title: Setting Resolution
docs.text:
Each setting is resolved in priority order:

  1. User override (stored in the database) — highest priority
  2. Tier default — based on your detected hardware tier
  3. Hardcoded fallback — always present as a baseline

Only user overrides are stored. Absence means "use the tier default."

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Setting Type Range Description embedding_batch_size int 1-128 Faces processed per GPU inference call frame_extraction_concurrency int 1-16 Parallel ffmpeg processes for frame extraction detection_size int 160-1280 Face detection input resolution (pixels) media_job_nice int 0-19 Nice level for ffmpeg run by CPU-heavy jobs (default 10; 19 yields to everything else) media_job_threads int 0-64 Thread cap per ffmpeg run by CPU-heavy jobs (default 0 = ffmpeg decides) content_index_workers int 1-16 Files the content index fingerprints at once (default 2)

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text: Setting Type Range Description stash_api_rate float 0.5-50 Max requests/second to local Stash instance

docs.title: Recognition
docs.text: Setting Type Range Description gpu_enabled bool - Use GPU for inference (disable to force CPU) num_frames int 10-200 Frames to sample per scene face_candidates int 5-100 Candidate matches retrieved from vector index per face

docs.title: Signals
