docs.text:
All critical fixes have been implemented in both the trainer and sidecar:

  1. Face alignment - Added InsightFace norm_crop 5-point similarity transform (trainer: 575525e, sidecar: 66d9ef8)
  2. ArcFace normalization - Fixed from x/255 to (x-127.5)/128 (trainer: ce06344, sidecar: 66d9ef8)
  3. Flip-averaging - Added horizontal flip embedding averaging (trainer: ce06344, sidecar: 66d9ef8)
  4. Aspect-ratio resize - Replaced stretching with aspect-ratio-preserving resize + black padding (trainer: ce06344, sidecar: 66d9ef8)
  5. Manifest updated - Reflects actual pipeline models (trainer: 2975e31)
  6. Nuke script - python -m api.nuke_enrichment_data --yes to clear all enrichment data (trainer: 259ebd3)

Next step: Run nuke script, then re-scrape with high-trust sources first (stashdb, theporndb), followed by reference sites and medium-trust sources. See plan's "Post-Implementation: Database Rebuild Instructions" section.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Face recognition results are extremely poor. The system fails to correctly identify performers even in controlled conditions (still photos from galleries) where identification should be trivial. Example: Gallery 2139 (Holly Randall shoot featuring Jayden Jaymes) - the system thinks there are multiple different people and doesn't rank Jayden Jaymes highly, despite her having multiple face embeddings in the database.

docs.title: Investigation Summary
docs.text: Root cause analysis traced the problem to two critical bugs in embeddings.py (shared between trainer and sidecar), plus several missing best practices that competitive systems implement.

docs.title: Bug 1: No Face Alignment (PRIMARY - ~70% of quality loss)
What's happening
docs.text:
In both stash-sense-trainer/api/embeddings.py and stash-sense/api/embeddings.py, the detect_faces() method crops faces using a raw bounding box with zero alignment:

# embeddings.py line 150 (trainer), line 150 (sidecar)
face_img = image[y1:y2, x1:x2]  # Raw bounding box crop

docs.title: What should happen
docs.text:
FaceNet512 and ArcFace were trained on aligned faces. Face alignment is a standard preprocessing step in face recognition where detected faces are rotated so that the eyes are horizontally level before cropping. This normalizes head pose and is critical for embedding consistency.

DeepFace's own extract_faces() function does this by default (align=True):

  1. Detect eye landmarks
  2. Calculate rotation angle: angle = degrees(arctan2(left_eye_y - right_eye_y, left_eye_x - right_eye_x))
  3. Apply 2D affine rotation via cv2.warpAffine() to make eyes horizontal
  4. Crop the aligned face

Our code already has the landmark data - InsightFace's RetinaFace provides 5-point facial landmarks (face.kps containing left_eye, right_eye, nose, mouth_left, mouth_right). We store them in DetectedFace.landmarks but never use them for alignment.

docs.title: Why this destroys quality
docs.text:
Without alignment, a 15-degree head tilt produces embeddings that are significantly different from the same person with a level head. The models never learned to be invariant to rotation because their training data was always pre-aligned. This means:

  • Different photos of the same person at different head angles produce widely scattered embeddings
  • The "centroid" of a performer's embedding cluster is noisy and unstable
  • Query-time embeddings from natural photos rarely land near the correct cluster

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: This is a well-established requirement in face recognition literature. Every competitive system does alignment: - StashFace (cc1234): Uses DeepFace's extract_faces() which has align=True by default - FaceStash (kozobot): Uses the face_recognition library which internally uses dlib's alignment - DeepFace itself: Alignment is ON by default in all pipelines - InsightFace's own recognition pipeline: Uses landmark-based alignment before embedding

docs.title: Bug 2: Wrong ArcFace Normalization (SECONDARY - ~30% of quality loss)
What's happening
docs.text:
# embeddings.py line 206 (trainer), line 206 (sidecar)
arcface_input = arcface_input / 255.0  # Produces [0, 1] range - WRONG

docs.title: What should happen
docs.text:
Per the ArcFace paper, DeepFace's own preprocessing code (preprocessing.py:66-71), and StashFace's implementation:

arcface_input = (arcface_input - 127.5) / 128  # Produces ~[-1, 1] range - CORRECT

The ArcFace model expects input pixels normalized to approximately [-0.996, 0.996] via (x - 127.5) / 128. Feeding [0, 1] range input shifts the entire activation distribution. The model still produces embeddings, but they're degraded - lower discriminative power.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• DeepFace source preprocessing.py line 66-71: img -= 127.5; img /= 128 for ArcFace normalization
  • ArcFace paper: "each pixel in RGB images is normalised by subtracting 127.5 then divided by 128"
  • StashFace uses preprocessing.normalize_input(resized, "ArcFace") which applies this correct normalization

docs.title: Additional FaceNet normalization concern
docs.text:
Our FaceNet normalization: 

facenet_input = (facenet_input - 127.5) / 127.5  # Our code

StashFace uses "Facenet2018" normalization which is: 

img /= 127.5  # Then img -= 1
# Equivalent to: (img - 127.5) / 127.5

These are mathematically equivalent, so our FaceNet normalization is correct.

docs.title: Issue 3: No Aspect-Ratio-Preserving Resize
docs.text:
Our code resizes faces by stretching to the target size:

pil_img = pil_img.resize(target_size, Image.Resampling.BILINEAR)  # Non-preserving stretch

DeepFace and StashFace use aspect-ratio-preserving resize with black padding:

# DeepFace preprocessing.resize_image()
factor = min(target_h / img_h, target_w / img_w)
resized = cv2.resize(img, (int(img_w * factor), int(img_h * factor)))
# Then pad with black to reach target_size

Impact: Moderate. Stretching distorts facial proportions slightly, adding noise to embeddings.

docs.title: Issue 4: No Horizontal Flip Augmentation at Query Time
docs.text:
StashFace's key technique: For every detected face, it generates embeddings for BOTH the original and a horizontally flipped version, then averages them:

face_batch = np.stack([face, face[:, ::-1, :]], axis=0)  # Original + flipped
embeddings_batch = ensemble.get_face_embeddings_batch(face_batch)
facenet = np.mean(embeddings_batch['facenet'], axis=0)  # Average
arc = np.mean(embeddings_batch['arc'], axis=0)           # Average

Why this helps: Faces are roughly symmetric. Averaging original + mirror embeddings: - Cancels out left-right asymmetries from lighting, expression, and slight pose - Produces a more "canonical" embedding closer to the center of the person's embedding cluster - Reduces the impact of minor alignment imperfections - Is essentially a free accuracy boost at the cost of 2x inference time

docs.title: Issue 5: E4M3 Quantized Storage (StashFace optimization)
docs.text: StashFace uses StorageDataType.E4M3 (8-bit float) for Voyager indices, reducing memory by 4x with minimal accuracy loss for cosine similarity. We use full 32-bit float. This is an optimization, not a bug - but worth considering for a 553K+ face database.

docs.title: Issue 6: Manifest Inconsistency
docs.text: The manifest says "detector": "yolov8" but the code uses buffalo_sc (InsightFace RetinaFace). Either the manifest is stale from a prior version, or a different detector was used for the current DB build. This should be clarified and fixed during the rebuild.

docs.title: Competitive Analysis: StashFace (cc1234)
docs.text:
StashFace is the primary competitive reference. Here's what it does right that we should match or exceed:

Feature StashFace Our System Gap Face alignment DeepFace extract_faces(align=True) None (raw crop) CRITICAL ArcFace normalization (x-127.5)/128 via DeepFace x/255 CRITICAL FaceNet normalization "Facenet2018" via DeepFace (x-127.5)/127.5 OK (equivalent) Horizontal flip averaging Yes (original + flipped, averaged) No HIGH Aspect-ratio resize Yes (DeepFace resize_image) No (stretch) Medium Index space Cosine Cosine OK Index storage E4M3 (8-bit) Float32 Low (optimization) Embedding dimensions 512 (both models) 512 (both models) OK Model weights Equal (1.0 each) FaceNet 0.6, ArcFace 0.4 Tuning difference Face detection YOLOv8 + MediaPipe InsightFace RetinaFace Different but OK Database size ~130K performers ~70K performers Different scope Confidence scoring Softmax with temperature + boost Linear (1 - distance) Different approach

docs.title: Phase 1: Fix embeddings.py (both trainer and sidecar)
1a. Add face alignment using InsightFace landmarks
docs.text:
Use the 5-point landmarks already available from RetinaFace to align faces before cropping. The alignment should:

  1. Get left_eye and right_eye coordinates from face.kps[0] and face.kps[1]
  2. Calculate rotation angle to make eyes horizontal
  3. Apply affine rotation via cv2.warpAffine()
  4. Crop the aligned face

This approach is simpler and faster than DeepFace's alignment because we already have reliable landmarks from RetinaFace (no need for a separate eye detector).

For even better alignment, consider using InsightFace's built-in norm_crop() which does a 5-point affine alignment (not just rotation but also scaling and translation to place landmarks at standard positions). This is what InsightFace's own ArcFace model was trained with and would produce the best-aligned faces.

docs.title: 1b. Fix ArcFace normalization
docs.text: Change from / 255.0 to (x - 127.5) / 128.

docs.title: 1c. Add aspect-ratio-preserving resize
docs.text: Use either DeepFace's preprocessing.resize_image() directly, or implement equivalent logic with OpenCV/PIL that resizes maintaining aspect ratio and pads with black.

docs.title: 1d. Add horizontal flip averaging
docs.text: Generate embeddings for both the original face and its horizontal mirror, then average both vectors. This provides a free accuracy boost.

docs.title: Phase 2: Rebuild the face database
docs.text:
Since embeddings.py is shared between trainer and sidecar:

  1. Keep all performer metadata - names, aliases, stashbox IDs, countries, etc. are all correct
  2. Keep all face image URLs - we know which images to download for each performer
  3. Delete all face embeddings and Voyager index entries
  4. Run a new enrichment pass to re-detect faces, align them, and generate correct embeddings
  5. Export new faces.json, performers.json, and Voyager indices

The trainer's face URLs are stored in the faces table's image_url column. We can reprocess these same URLs with the corrected pipeline rather than re-scraping from stashbox. This means: - No stashbox API rate limiting concerns - Much faster than original scraping (just downloading images and processing) - Same curated image set, just better embeddings

docs.title: Phase 3: Update sidecar embeddings.py
docs.text: Copy the corrected embeddings.py from the trainer to the sidecar. Since they're supposed to be identical (the trainer file says "this file is shared"), this ensures query-time preprocessing matches DB build-time preprocessing exactly.

docs.title: Phase 4: Update matching/scoring (optional improvements)
docs.text: After the critical fixes, consider: - Tuning fusion weights (StashFace uses equal 1.0/1.0 instead of our 0.6/0.4) - Implementing softmax-based confidence scoring instead of linear - Adding E4M3 quantized storage for memory efficiency - Re-evaluating health detection thresholds (may not trigger as often with correct embeddings)

docs.title: Will this fix the problem?
docs.text: Very high confidence (95%+). The alignment issue alone accounts for most face recognition systems' accuracy. It's the single most important preprocessing step in face recognition, and we completely skip it. Every working system we examined does alignment.

docs.title: Will we match or exceed StashFace?
docs.text:
Yes. After implementing all Phase 1 fixes, our system will use: - The same models (FaceNet512 + ArcFace) - The same distance metric (Cosine) - The same preprocessing (alignment + correct normalization + flip averaging) - A comparable database size (70K performers) - More sophisticated matching (dual-model health detection and adaptive fusion)

Our health detection and adaptive fusion strategy is actually more sophisticated than StashFace's simple weighted voting, which should give us an edge in edge cases.

docs.title: What about InsightFace's built-in ArcFace?
docs.text: InsightFace ships with its own ArcFace recognition model (e.g., w600k_r50 in the buffalo_l model pack). This is a different ArcFace implementation than DeepFace's, trained on a larger dataset (WebFace600K vs MS1M). We could potentially add it as a third signal or replace DeepFace's ArcFace entirely. However, this would be a larger change and the fixes above should already bring us to competitive quality.

docs.title: Trainer (stash-sense-trainer)
docs.text:
• api/embeddings.py - Add alignment, fix normalization, add flip averaging
  • api/face_processor.py - May need updates for new preprocessing
  • api/index_manager.py - No changes needed (Cosine space is correct)
  • Database: Delete face rows + re-populate via enrichment run

docs.title: Sidecar (stash-sense)
docs.text:
• api/embeddings.py - Mirror all changes from trainer
  • api/matching.py - Consider weight tuning after rebuild
  • api/recognizer.py - No structural changes needed

docs.title: Appendix: How StashFace's Pipeline Works (Complete)
docs.text:
For reference, here's StashFace's complete pipeline as reverse-engineered from the source:

INPUT IMAGE
    |
[YOLOv8 Face Detection] or [MediaPipe Face Detection]
    |
[DeepFace extract_faces(align=True)]
    |--- Eye landmark detection
    |--- 2D affine rotation to level eyes
    |--- Crop aligned face
    |
[For each detected face]
    |
    +-- [Create batch: original + horizontal flip]
    |       face_batch = stack([face, face[:, ::-1, :]])
    |
    +-- [FaceNet512 Preprocessing]
    |       resize_image(face, (160,160))  # aspect-ratio preserving + pad
    |       normalize_input(img, "Facenet2018")  # (x/127.5) - 1
    |       model(batch, training=False)
    |
    +-- [ArcFace Preprocessing]
    |       resize_image(face, (112,112))  # aspect-ratio preserving + pad
    |       normalize_input(img, "ArcFace")  # (x-127.5)/128
    |       model(batch, training=False)
    |
    +-- [Average original + flipped embeddings per model]
    |       facenet_emb = mean(facenet_batch, axis=0)
    |       arcface_emb = mean(arcface_batch, axis=0)
    |
    +-- [Query Voyager Indices (Cosine, E4M3)]
    |       facenet_results = index.query(facenet_emb, k=50)
    |       arcface_results = index.query(arcface_emb, k=50)
    |
    +-- [Ensemble Fusion]
    |       Weighted voting (1.0 each model)
    |       Softmax confidence with temperature
    |       Final score = normalized_votes * avg_confidence * boost
    |
OUTPUT: Ranked performer matches with confidence scores

docs.title: Face recognition failure analysis (#139)
docs.text:
The 2026-02-12 re-evaluation left scene accuracy near 42% and could not say why performers are missed. This benchmark runs the production scene pipeline over about 200 of your own scenes and gives every missed performer one reason. That tells us whether detection, frame choice or matching loses the most, which decides whether #140 (pose-guided frame selection) is next.

Code: api/benchmark/failure/. Data and results live under $DATA_DIR/benchmark/ (/data/benchmark/ in the container), never in the repo, because the scene list is personal.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
Run it inside the sidecar container, which has the GPU, the current face DB and (with MEDIA_PATH_MAP set) the media mount.

# 1. Freeze a benchmark set (once). 200 scenes, seed 139, stratified by era x resolution.
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure build-set

# 2. Run: writes raw/<scene>.json per scene, then report.md and summary.json.
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure run

# Smoke test first if you like
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure run --limit 3

# Resume an interrupted run
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure run --resume /data/benchmark/runs/<run_id>

# Re-score a run with other thresholds (no GPU work)
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure report /data/benchmark/runs/<run_id> --attribution 0.55 --suffix -strict

docker exec runs as root (it skips the entrypoint's drop to PUID), which keeps the InsightFace cache at /root/.insightface visible. Files it writes under /data/benchmark are handed back to PUID:PGID the next time the container starts. The run loads its own copy of the models, so it uses GPU memory alongside the sidecar. Pipeline settings (num_frames, detection_size, frame extraction workers) come from the sidecar's saved settings, the same values /identify/scene uses, and are recorded in meta.json.

docs.title: What a scene qualifies as
docs.text: A StashDB-linked scene with a dated file, at least one performer, and every performer linked to StashDB. That last rule makes the expected set complete, so false positives are real. Eras: pre-2010, 2010-2014, 2015-2019, 2020+. Resolution by the file's short side: SD (< 720), 720p, 1080p (including 1440p), 4K. Each stratum gets an equal share of the 200, and shares a small stratum can't fill pass to the others.

docs.title: How a scene is scored
docs.text:
The run calls the same code as POST /identify/scene in frequency mode: evenly spaced frames, RetinaFace detection, size filter, batch embedding plus index match (scene_matcher.recognize_detected_faces), the upscaled screenshot, then clustered_frequency_matching. Two deliberate differences:

  • No tagged-performer boost. The plugin sends the scene's tagged performers, which here are the answer key.
  • No body or tattoo re-ranking. This measures the face pipeline.

A performer counts as found when a person with frame_count > 1 has them as best match. That is the plugin's main group; single-frame persons sit in a collapsed section. A false positive is a multi-frame person matched to someone not in the scene. Identity is compared by performer, so a match keyed by any of their stash-box ids counts.

docs.title: Miss reasons
docs.text:
For each scene face, the run also computes its fused distance to every expected performer's own DB faces (gallery.py, the same weighted FaceNet plus ArcFace cosine production uses). A face is attributed to a performer when that distance is at most 0.65 and no other expected performer is closer. Attribution uses the answer key and only explains misses.

Checked in order, first hit wins:

Reason Meaning not_in_db No faces for the performer in the face DB no_face_detected No detected face is attributed to them dropped_by_aggregation They were top-1 (within max_distance) on at least one face production saw, but scene aggregation didn't report them as a multi-frame person small_or_profile Every attributed face is under 80 px on the short side or turned past 45 degrees yaw wrong_match A usable face of theirs was detected and embedded, and someone else won it (distance to the right answer and the winner are recorded)

dropped_by_aggregation goes beyond the issue's four reasons. The re-eval found that min_unique_frames 2 to 1 recovered 9 of 28 misses, so per-face correct matches lost in aggregation are common, and folding them into wrong_match would hide a cheap fix.

docs.title: Frame choice vs detection: the keyframe probe
docs.text:
"No face detected in the sampled frames" can't tell a detector miss from a bad pick of frames on its own. For no_face_detected and small_or_profile misses, the run decodes the scene's keyframes (up to 400, evenly thinned, keyframes only so it's cheap) and looks for a face that is attributed to the performer, at least 80 px, frontal, and matched top-1 to them. The outcome maps each miss to a stage:

Stage Misses counted frame_choice No face or small/profile in the samples, but a keyframe elsewhere has a usable, correctly matched face detection_or_absent No face detected, and no keyframe has one either size_or_pose_throughout Small/profile in the samples, and never usable anywhere matching wrong_match + dropped_by_aggregation db_coverage not_in_db unprobed Probe didn't run (no local file and no --probe-stream, --no-probe, or an error)

The probe reads the whole file, so by default it only runs on local files from the media mount. --probe-stream allows it over Stash's HTTP stream.

The verdict line names the stage with the most misses. frame_choice points at #140.

docs.title: Detection test set
docs.text:
This measures detector recall on SD footage independently of recognition, which is what detection_or_absent needs to be read correctly.

# Sample 300 SD frames from the benchmark set and pre-draw boxes with a high-recall detector
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure detect-sample

# Label: copy /data/benchmark/detection to a machine with a browser and run the labeler there
# (stdlib only, no ML deps), then copy labels.json back.
cd api && python -m benchmark.failure label --dir <copy>    # http://localhost:8139

# Score the production detector against your labels
docker exec stash-sense python -m benchmark.failure detect-score

InsightFace's RetinaFace expects BGR input (it calls blobFromImage(..., swapRB=True)). Until #147 the sidecar and the trainer fed it RGB. On this set, RGB gave 72.2% recall and 99.2% precision, and BGR gave 75.3% and 97.8%. Both now feed it BGR and still align crops from the RGB image, so embeddings are unchanged. detect-score scores production (BGR) by default; --channel-order rgb reproduces the old input.

Labeling policy: box every human face where at least one eye is visible, any size, any angle. Accept a frame with no boxes if it has no faces. The score reports recall by face size (< 40, 40-79, 80+ px), precision, and "usable recall" (detected and large enough to pass the production size filter).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
/data/benchmark/runs/<run_id>/:

  • meta.json: DB version, resolved pipeline settings, set seed
  • raw/<scene_id>.json: every face (box, yaw, detection score, top 5 matches, distance to each expected performer), the persons production returned, probe verdicts
  • summary.json: totals, reason and stage counts, per-stratum tables, wrong-match distance stats, attribution sensitivity at 0.55, 0.65 and 0.75, and one outcome per expected performer
  • report.md: the same, readable

Compare runs across changes by diffing summary.json, or re-score older raw data with report.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
New face recognition database imported from stash-sense-trainer with: - 107,759 performers, 277,097 faces from 5 sources (stashdb, fansdb, theporndb, pmvstash, javstash) - Proper face alignment (insightface_norm_crop_5point) - previously raw bbox crops - Correct ArcFace normalization ((x-127.5)/128) - previously /255 - Flip averaging for embeddings

Previous testing (Feb 4-6) used garbage data and yielded ~44% accuracy, ~31% precision at best.

docs.title: Test Setup
docs.text:
• 20 stratified test scenes (15x 1080p, 5x 720p)
  • 48 expected performers across all scenes
  • All scenes classified as "sparse" coverage tier
  • Benchmark script: api/benchmark/reeval.py
  • Full JSON results: api/benchmark_results/reeval_20260212_064023.json
  • Runtime: 166 minutes

docs.title: Phase 1: Baseline (Current Defaults)
docs.text:
Metric Value Accuracy 41.7% Precision 32.8% TP / Expected 20 / 48 False Positives 41 1080p accuracy 39.5% 720p accuracy 50.0%

Key finding: Accuracy is roughly the same as old DB (~44%). The alignment/normalization fixes didn't meaningfully improve scene identification. The bottleneck is elsewhere in the pipeline.

docs.title: max_distance - No impact above 0.5
docs.text:
max_distance Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 0.3 4.2% 100.0% 2 0 46 0.4 33.3% 43.2% 16 21 32 0.5 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 0.6 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 0.7 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 0.8 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 0.9 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28

Insight: Matches either land below 0.5 or don't land at all. Anything above 0.5 is noise. Can safely tighten to 0.5.

docs.title: min_face_size - No impact below 80
docs.text:
min_face_size Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 30 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 40 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 60 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 80 37.5% 36.7% 18 31 30 100 29.2% 32.6% 14 29 34

Insight: Below 80px there are no additional small faces being matched. Above 80 loses faces.

docs.title: fusion_weights - ArcFace now pulling its weight
docs.text:
Weights (fn/af) Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 0.7/0.3 39.6% 30.6% 19 43 29 0.6/0.4 (old default) 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 0.5/0.5 43.8% 33.9% 21 41 27 0.4/0.6 43.8% 32.8% 21 43 27 0.3/0.7 41.7% 31.2% 20 44 28

Insight: Equal weighting is optimal. This confirms the ArcFace normalization fix is working - it's now a reliable signal. The old 0.6/0.4 bias toward FaceNet was compensating for broken ArcFace.

docs.title: matching_mode - Frequency wins
docs.text:
Mode Accuracy Precision TP FP FN frequency 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 hybrid 39.6% 33.9% 19 37 29

Insight: Hybrid has marginally better precision (fewer FPs) but loses 1 TP. Frequency is the better default.

docs.title: min_appearances - No meaningful impact
docs.text:
min_appearances Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 1 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 2 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 3 39.6% 47.5% 19 21 29

Insight: 1→2 identical. 3 is a strong precision filter (47.5%) at slight accuracy cost. Could be useful in a "high precision" mode.

docs.title: min_unique_frames - THE biggest lever (tied with num_frames)
docs.text:
min_unique_frames Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 1 60.4% 30.5% 29 66 19 2 (default) 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 3 31.2% 55.6% 15 12 33

Insight: Dropping from 2→1 recovers 9 TPs (+45% relative) but adds 25 FPs. The unique frame requirement is the binding constraint for many performers who only appear clearly in one frame. Setting to 3 gives 55.6% precision but kills recall.

docs.title: min_confidence - Zero impact
docs.text:
min_confidence Accuracy Precision 0.2 41.7% 32.8% 0.3 41.7% 32.8% 0.35 41.7% 32.8% 0.4 41.7% 32.8% 0.5 41.7% 32.8%

Insight: The confidence threshold is never the binding constraint. All matches that pass the distance filter also pass any confidence threshold we tested.

docs.title: num_frames - Strong positive correlation with accuracy
docs.text:
num_frames Accuracy Precision TP FP FN 20 35.4% 44.7% 17 21 31 40 (default) 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 60 54.2% 36.1% 26 46 22 80 60.4% 30.5% 29 66 19

Insight: Clear linear relationship. Each 20 extra frames adds ~6% accuracy. 60 is the best accuracy/precision/runtime balance: +12.5% accuracy over baseline, precision actually improves to 36.1%, and only 50% more runtime than 40 frames. 80 frames has diminishing returns and drops precision.

docs.title: Phase 3: Best-of Combination
docs.text:
Combined best from each sweep: 

max_distance=0.5, min_face_size=30, fn/af=0.5/0.5,
matching_mode=frequency, min_appearances=1, min_unique_frames=1,
min_confidence=0.2, num_frames=80

Config Accuracy Precision TP FP FN Baseline 41.7% 32.8% 20 41 28 Best combo 62.5% 30.0% 30 70 18 Delta +20.8% -2.8% +10 +29 -10

The gains come primarily from more frames + dropping min_unique_frames to 1.

docs.title: Phase 4: Original Scene Re-validation (8 scenes)
docs.text:
Config Accuracy Precision TP FP FN Default params 50.0% 26.7% 8 22 8 Best params 56.2% 22.5% 9 31 7

Per-scene: - Scene 13938 (1080p): 2/2 both configs - Scene 16342 (1080p): 2/2 both configs - Scene 30835 (1080p): 0/2 both configs - stubborn failure - Scene 3283 (720p): 0/2 → 1/2 (best params recovered one) - Others: 1/2 both configs

docs.title: Phase 5: Gallery Benchmark
docs.text:
10 galleries tested, 5 distance thresholds. Results were nearly identical across all thresholds:

max_distance Accuracy Precision TP FP FN All (0.4-0.8) 78.3% 3.6% 18 483-488 5

Major problem: Gallery 1062 (1,074 images, 2 expected performers) generated 279-283 FPs alone. Excluding it, the other 9 galleries had ~204 FPs for 16 TPs (~7.3% precision).

Root cause: The "2+ appearances OR single < 0.4" aggregation filter is far too permissive for galleries. Each face in each image produces a top-1 match, and with hundreds of images, random performers easily get 2+ appearances.

Suggested fixes for gallery aggregation: 1. Require appearances in minimum % of images (e.g., 10%) not just absolute count 2. Scale minimum appearances with gallery size (e.g., max(2, image_count * 0.05)) 3. Use stricter distance thresholds for gallery mode 4. Require the performer to be the top-1 match (not just any match) in multiple images

docs.title: Phase 6: Image Benchmark
docs.text: Skipped - no images in the library had tagged performers with StashDB IDs.

docs.title: Applied Parameter Changes
docs.text:
Based on these findings, the following "safe" changes were applied:

Parameter Old Default New Default Rationale facenet_weight 0.6 0.5 ArcFace now working correctly, equal weighting optimal arcface_weight 0.4 0.5 Same max_distance 0.7 0.5 Results plateau at 0.5, tighter = less noise num_frames 40 60 +12.5% accuracy, best precision of elevated frame counts

Not changed (needs further investigation): - min_unique_frames: kept at 2 (dropping to 1 has huge FP cost) - min_appearances: kept at 2 - min_confidence: kept at 0.35 (no impact either way)

docs.title: Problem: Flat Frequency Matching Produces Too Many "Persons"
docs.text: The frequency matching mode had no concept of face clustering - it threw all face detections into a flat bag and counted performer appearances. A 2-person scene with 38 face detections would produce 34 "persons" in the UI, one per unique performer match.

docs.title: Root Cause: L2 Distance on Concatenated Embeddings
docs.text: The existing cluster_faces_by_person used L2 distance on concatenated 1024-dim (FaceNet+ArcFace) embeddings with threshold 0.6. In that high-dimensional space, same-person faces are typically 1.0+ apart in L2 distance, so the 0.6 threshold was far too tight and almost no clustering happened.

docs.title: Fix: Clustered Frequency Matching
docs.text:
Implemented a two-stage approach (clustered_frequency_matching):

  1. Stage 1 - Clustering: Group faces by cosine similarity (consistent with Voyager indices) using pre-computed embeddings (avoids recomputing). Threshold 0.6 cosine distance works well.
  2. Stage 2 - Identification: Within each cluster, run frequency-style matching to identify who each person is. Alternatives shown per cluster.

Also merged clusters with the same best match (existing merge_clusters_by_match).

docs.title: Results
docs.text: Scene Faces Old Persons New Persons Correct Top Matches 709 38 34 9 (2 dominant: 22 + 5 frames) Rilynn Rae, Keiran Lee 14650 34 ~30 2 Ella Reese, Tim Gottfrid 19759 94 ~80 6 (4 dominant: 27+24+20+17 frames) Karlie Montana, Madison Ivy, Keiran Lee, Voodoo

docs.title: Additional Improvements
docs.text:
• Tagged-performer awareness: Plugin sends existing scene performer StashDB IDs to the API. A small confidence boost (+0.03) is applied to already-tagged performers, and already_tagged flag is returned for UI display.
  • "Already tagged" UI state: Shows "Already tagged on scene" with green badge instead of "Add to Scene" button for performers already on the scene.
  • Grouped UI: Multi-frame clusters shown prominently; single-frame detections collapsed in a collapsible section.
  • Embedding reuse: RecognitionResult now stores the pre-computed embedding, eliminating redundant embedding generation during clustering.

docs.title: Future Investigation Areas
docs.text:
1. Why is accuracy still ~42% with good embeddings? The database quality improvement didn't help scenes. Investigate whether the problem is face detection (faces not being detected), frame selection (wrong moments), or matching (wrong performers winning).

  2. Failure analysis on specific performers: Which of the 28 FN performers are being missed and why? Are they in the database? Are their faces being detected? Are they being matched to wrong performers?

  3. Scene 30835: Consistently 0/2 across all parameter configs. What's special about this scene?

  4. Gallery aggregation redesign: Current "2+ appearances" filter is broken for galleries. Need percentage-based or statistical approach.

  5. min_unique_frames=1 with compensating FP filter: Could we drop to 1 frame but add a stricter distance threshold (e.g., require distance < 0.4 for single-frame matches)?

  6. Image benchmark: Need to tag some images with performers to enable Phase 6.

  7. Larger scene sample: 20 scenes with 48 performers is small. Results can shift by 1-2 TPs. Consider running with 50+ scenes for more statistical power.

docs.title: Split regression (#131)
docs.text:
This is the split planner (api/splits/planner.py) run on every title of the regression set and scored against the owner's labelled cuts. The set is api/tests/fixtures/split_regression/: index.jsonl holds one record per title (anonymized id, series label, duration, the labelled cuts, whether the owner left it whole, and the labelled keep_until), and <id>.npz the extracted video and audio signals. The report holds only fixture ids, series labels and numbers.

Each title is planned leave-one-out: its profile is built (profiles.build_profile) from the other titles of its series that have labelled cuts, using features_at on their labelled cuts, with each title's total taken as its labelled keep_until when it has one and its duration otherwise. A series with no other labelled title, or a profile with fewer than 3 boundaries, gives no profile (the planner then gives at most medium, unless coverage confirms the plan).

Decision 2026-11-18: high needs a fade-type series profile (black rate >= 0.75) or confirmed coverage. The relaxed fallback and the no-profile rule were removed after the first run showed 9 of 12 high plans missing labels.

Terms:

  • exact: the plan has as many cuts as the label and every cut is within 2 s of its label.
  • recall: the share of labelled cuts that have a plan cut within 2 s (or 30 s). Median distance is from each labelled cut to the nearest plan cut, over the labelled cuts of the plans in that row that have one.
  • at a black start: a dark run (detect.dark_runs) starts within 0.5 s of the labelled cut. Some labels were never snapped to a black start: titles with static transitions (owner scrub times, which land a few seconds after the first static burst) and a few labels from before the cut-at-black-start rule (they sit mid-black). In the tables a label that is not at a black start is marked *. This column is for reading only; the pass/fail rule does not use it.

Titles: 118 (109 labelled, 9 left whole). Labelled cuts: 558, of which 271/558 (48.6%) are at a black start.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• NVIDIA GPU (GTX 10-series or newer recommended)
  • Unraid 6.12+

docs.title: Step 1: Install Nvidia Driver Plugin
docs.text:
1. Go to Apps → Search "Nvidia Driver"
  2. Install Nvidia-Driver by ich777
  3. Reboot Unraid

docs.title: Step 3: Container Configuration
docs.text:
The Stash Sense template automatically includes GPU settings.

If configuring manually, ensure these are set:

Setting Value Extra Parameters --runtime=nvidia --gpus all NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES all (or specific GPU UUID)

docs.title: "nvidia-smi: command not found"
docs.text:
Driver plugin not installed or Unraid needs reboot.

# Check if plugin is installed
ls /boot/config/plugins/nvidia-driver.plg
# If missing, reinstall from Apps

docs.title: "No GPU detected in container"
docs.text:
Check container has GPU access:

docker exec stash-sense nvidia-smi

If this fails, verify:

  1. Extra Parameters includes --runtime=nvidia
  2. Container was recreated after driver install (not just restarted)

docs.title: "CUDA out of memory"
docs.text:
Another process is using the GPU. Check what's using it:

nvidia-smi

Look at "Processes" section. Common culprits: - Plex hardware transcoding - Tdarr - Frigate - Other ML containers

docs.title: "Failed to initialize NVML"
docs.text: The Nvidia container toolkit isn't configured. Re-install the driver plugin and reboot.

docs.title: Selecting a Specific GPU (Multi-GPU Systems)
docs.text:
If you have multiple GPUs, specify which one to use:

# List GPU UUIDs
nvidia-smi -L

# Use specific GPU
NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

Or by index: 

NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0  # First GPU
NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1  # Second GPU

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Unraid 6.12+
  • Nvidia Driver plugin installed (for GPU acceleration)
  • Stash running on Unraid or accessible from Unraid

docs.title: 1. Download the template
docs.text:
Copy stash-sense.xml to your Unraid flash drive:

/boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/stash-sense.xml

docs.title: 2. Add container
docs.text: Go to Docker → Add Container → Template → User Templates → stash-sense

docs.title: 3. Configure
docs.text:
Setting Value Stash URL http://stash:9999 or your Stash IP/hostname Stash API Key From Stash: Settings → Security → API Key Data Directory Path to extracted database files Media Library The share Stash reads your videos from. Keep Access Mode Read Only unless you enable a feature that writes files (subtitles) MEDIA_PATH_MAP stash_path=/media. If Stash's template maps your library to /data, use /data=/media PUID / PGID 99 / 100 (unRAID's nobody:users); files the sidecar creates get this owner

To keep CPU-heavy jobs off some cores, add --cpuset-cpus=2-7 (your core list) to Extra Parameters. After starting, the plugin's Settings tab shows the GPU tier and each media mount with its mode.

docs.title: 4. Apply
docs.text: Click Apply. The container will download and start.

docs.title: Option 2: Docker Compose
docs.text: If you prefer docker-compose on Unraid:

docs.title: 1. Create directory
docs.text: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/stash-sense

docs.title: 2. Create docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
version: "3.8"

services:
  stash-sense:
    image: carrotwaxr/stash-sense:latest
    container_name: stash-sense
    runtime: nvidia
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6960:5000"
    environment:
      - STASH_URL=http://stash:9999
      - STASH_API_KEY=your-api-key
      - NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all
      - PUID=99
      - PGID=100
      - MEDIA_PATH_MAP=/data=/media
    volumes:
      - /mnt/user/appdata/stash-sense/data:/data
      - /mnt/user/appdata/stash-sense/models:/root/.insightface
      - /mnt/user/media:/media:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu]

docs.title: 3. Start
docs.text:
cd /mnt/user/appdata/stash-sense
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Database Setup
docs.text:
Download the database release and extract:

cd /mnt/user/appdata/stash-sense/data
wget https://github.com/carrotwaxr/stash-sense/releases/download/db-latest/stash-sense-db.tar.gz
tar -xzf stash-sense-db.tar.gz
rm stash-sense-db.tar.gz

You should have: 

data/
├── face_facenet.voy
├── face_arcface.voy
├── performers.json
└── manifest.json

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
If Stash runs on the same Unraid server, use Docker's internal networking:

  • Stash URL: http://stash:9999 (if Stash container is named "stash")
  • Or use Unraid's IP: http://192.168.1.x:9999
